validity.researcher_notes: The Haynesville/Perryville Expansion is a compression-only capacity addition, not new mainline pipe. Federal Register Docket No. CP09-420-000 (Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP application, May 22, 2009): 'authorization to construct, install, own, operate and maintain three new compressor units and yard and station piping ... at two existing Gulf South compressor stations ... the Hall Summit Compressor Station, Bienville Parish, Louisiana, where two new turbine compressor units totaling 32,913 horsepower (HP) are proposed, and at the Tallulah Compressor Station, Madison Parish, Louisiana, where one new 17,558 hp turbine compressor unit is proposed' (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2009/06/15/E9-13960/gulf-south-pipeline-company-lp-notice-of-application, verified 200/contains 'Hall Summit'). Tallulah Compressor Station sits at Perryville, LA and Hall Summit sits in the Haynesville-producing area, matching the sheet's SegmentName and StartState/Province=Louisiana. Construction completed October 2010, matching StartYear1=2010. The only pipe mentioned is 'yard and station piping' (incidental compressor-station plumbing, not a mainline segment with a route diameter), consistent with the sheet's own LengthKnownKm=0.00 already recorded by an earlier leg. Per the compression-only-expansion rule (gotcha 3), the blank Diameter is correct. Second source attempted (naturalgasintel.com's 'FERC OKs Second Major Expansion of Gulf South Pipe', which a web search snippet also describes as Hall Summit/Tallulah compression completing October 2010) is paywalled behind a login wall on direct fetch (curl 200 but article body absent; archive.org was returning 'Temporarily Offline' site-wide at time of research, so no Wayback fallback available) — I could not independently verify its text, so it is not cited and tier is held at medium on the one verified FERC filing.
